Korean Potato Salad

Korean potato salad is what happened when Western salad met the Korean banchan table: mashed potato bound lightly with mayo and fruit — apple, sometimes raisins or cucumber — sweet, soft, and completely unbothered by…

Korean · Easy · Serves 6–8 as banchan

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: contemporary — the Western-contact bowl, claimed. Korean potato salad is what happened when Western salad met the Korean banchan table: mashed potato bound lightly with mayo and fruit — apple, sometimes raisins or cucumber — sweet, soft, and completely unbothered by anyone's definition of salad. It arrived in the twentieth century, stayed for the children, and every Korean grill restaurant now serves it (#B22's macaroni sibling beside it). Labeled honestly as the modern bowl it is; loved without reservation, because it works.

The potatoes
The bind and the mix-ins

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • Boil the potato chunks 18–20 minutes to fully tender (a knife slides through the center piece with zero catch), drain, and let them steam dry in the pot 5 minutes — wet potato makes gluey salad.
  • Salt the diced cucumber 10 minutes and squeeze it — the #B07 law again; raw cucumber water is the bowl's sogginess clock, and squeezing resets it.
  • Boil the eggs while the potatoes go.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    Rice the potatoes or mash them coarse — deliberately coarse, with visible small chunks left in. Korean potato salad is not a smooth puree; the texture target is "mostly mashed, part smashed," with bits that keep the bowl interesting. Checkpoint — the mash holds a spoon's trail briefly and no water pools at the bowl's edge (if it does, the dry-steam was skipped — work quickly now, the mayo comes later).
  2. 02
    Fold while just-warm — this is the timing law: the sugar, salt, and about two-thirds of the mayo folded into warm potato (it melts in and seasons evenly), then the apple, squeezed cucumber, eggs, and scallion folded in as it cools. Checkpoint — the fold test at the end: the mix-ins distribute without mashing further, and every spoonful carries apple and egg — it should look generous, not potato-with-flecks.
  3. 03
    Chill 30 minutes minimum — the bowl is served cold, and the flavors need the chill to marry. The remaining mayo over the top, a grind of pepper. Checkpoint — the eating test, cold: soft-sweet, the apple's crisp-sweet snap and the cucumber's cool, the egg's richness, mayo's tang behind everything — a children's champion with a grown-up following, and the perfect cooling counter at a heavy grill table. Chef’s Note — Kewpie matters here in a way brand-loyalty usually doesn't deserve: it is made with only yolks and rice vinegar and MSG, and its richer, sweeter, tangier character is the flavor this salad's fans remember tasting — Hellmann's-bound versions taste like someone else's potato salad wearing the same clothes. If Kewpie is genuinely unavailable, add a pinch of sugar and a few drops of rice vinegar to regular mayo and get three-quarters of the way there.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Gluey, paste textureOver-mashed or wet potatoCoarse mash; the 5-minute dry-steam
Watery by next dayUnsqueezed cucumberThe salt-and-squeeze, always
BlandUnder-salted and under-sweetThe sugar is load-bearing; taste cold
Apple brownedDressed too warm, sat longFold the apple in as it cools; serve within a day

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Keeps 2 days refrigerated (the cucumber's clock) — a picnic and lunchbox staple by tradition.
  • Variations: raisins or canned fruit cocktail folded in (the old-school café build, sweeter than modern taste but the grandmothers' original); the macaroni sibling (#B22); a layer of the salad inside a gimbap roll — its most beloved deployment.
